claims.text: The studied material is HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Advanced atomistic or mesoscale simulations can accurately predict lattice heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Advanced atomistic or mesoscale simulations can accurately predict electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Molecular dynamics or Monte Carlo methods can account for complex atomic-scale interactions and defects in the material.
The proposed predictive approach is applicable from 200 K to 1200 K.
Atomic-scale interactions and defects influence lattice heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Atomic-scale interactions and defects influence electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed simulations would improve predictive understanding relative to available analytical approaches.
Available analytical approaches fail to capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity.
Quantitative heat-transport prediction remains uncertain because of material complexity and limitations of current analytical approaches.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing predicted lattice and electronic transport coefficients and temperature-dependent conductivity with low- and high-temperature measurements.
A significant deviation between predictions and experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability begins at 200 K, but the proposed falsification invokes low-temperature measurements without defining whether measurements below 200 K—central to the query—are outside the model's boundary.
